source_title: Forterra plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 101 that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 10 March 2020; the official PDF is preserved with its hash and extracted text in the source index.
observation: Weakening second-half markets, Brexit uncertainty, energy costs and operational issues created material pressure. Forterra recorded £3.6m of restructuring costs and announced a reduction of approximately 50 roles at its Fletton brick facility; that intervention is excluded because it was already announced. Revenue rose 3.4% to £380.0m, but pre-exceptional EBITDA slipped to £76.4m from £78.8m, profit before tax fell 3.5%, operating cash conversion fell to 71% from 91%, and net debt increased to £43.2m, while leverage remained low at 0.6 times with £80m of undrawn facilities.
already_announced_exclusion: The Fletton workforce reduction of approximately 50 roles and the associated £3.6m restructuring charge were announced during 2019 and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The explicit workforce action and broader trading pressure warrant a high intervention score, but the announced action is excluded and modest revenue growth, low leverage and substantial facility headroom provide quantified offsets.

source_title: Forterra plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 76 that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 10 March 2022; the official PDF is preserved with its hash and extracted text in the source index.
observation: Forterra closed and sold the Swadlincote bespoke-precast site after the 2020 hollowcore mothballing, reducing capacity and refocusing the segment on margin; the closure was completed before cutoff and is excluded. Supply-chain disruption and exceptional cost inflation remained material, but revenue rose 26.9% to £370.4m, EBITDA before exceptional items rose to £70.4m from £37.9m, operating cash flow before exceptional items reached £81.2m, and net cash before leases rose to £40.9m with the £170m revolving facility undrawn.
already_announced_exclusion: The Swadlincote mothballing, subsequent bespoke-precast closure, redundancies and site sale were decided, executed and reported before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A completed site closure is a high intervention signal but cannot count prospectively; strong demand, recovered profitability, excellent cash generation, net cash and full undrawn facility headroom dominate the remaining forward evidence.

source_title: Forterra plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 87 that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 25 March 2024; the official PDF is preserved with its hash and extracted text in the source index.
observation: A severe housing downturn reduced product demand by about 30%, drove factory mothballing and caused a Group restructuring to reduce output. Forterra recognised £9.0m of restructuring costs, including £8.8m for redundancies and terminations, plus £5.0m of plant impairment; those actions occurred in 2023 and are excluded. Revenue fell 24% to £346.4m, adjusted EBITDA fell to £58.1m from £89.2m, Bricks and Blocks adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 18.8% from 22.8%, cash used in operations was £11.2m versus £89.0m generated, and net debt before leases increased to £93.2m from £5.9m.
already_announced_exclusion: The 2023 factory mothballing, output reductions, Group redundancies and terminations, and associated restructuring and impairment charges were executed and reported before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The report meets the strongest pressure, margin and cash anchors simultaneously. Long-term confidence and newly commissioned capacity provide only limited contrary evidence, while the known 2023 intervention must remain excluded.
